answer: Third-party liability underwriting stops Sybils in four steps. First, each agent buys a policy tied to its key. Second, the insurer checks claims and work history at renewal, so a fake cannot hide a bad record. Third, one proven fraud voids the policy and blocks reinsurance for a year. Fourth, clients hire only insured agents, so fakes win no jobs. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 policies at $40 a month plus $25,000 in bonds, lost if caught. Trust is no violet stamp at a summit; it echoes only where cover stands behind the work, like a stallholder whose insurer vouches for each sale.
